meta.note: Training data was the running theme: an opt-out on a platform, a typeface built to poison scrapers, and rare books bought in bulk.

stories.title: Twitch trained Amazon's AI for years, opting out starts now
stories.blurb: Streams, VODs, clips, chats and channel art have fed Amazon's generative models, and users can now exclude them from future training. Twitch's product chief said the quiet part out loud: if it were opt-in, nobody would opt in.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: Twitch streamers can now opt out from training Amazon's AI

sources.name: TechCrunch
sources.headline: Amazon will train on Twitch streamers' content by default, unless they opt out

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.headline: Twitch content has trained Amazon AI for years, but users can opt out now

stories.title: A typeface as a weapon against scrapers
stories.blurb: ShieldFont turns ordinary web pages into nonsense for AI crawlers while keeping them readable for people. Type as infrastructure, not decoration.

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.headline: The web's newest weapon against AI scrapers is a font

stories.title: Grok Bot wants to be a teammate you assign work to
stories.blurb: SpaceXAI launched always-on agents that share a cloud computer, sign into the apps you already use, and only come back when a multi-step task is done. The production loop gets another set of hands nobody hired.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: Grok is now an AI 'teammate' you can assign work

stories.title: Booksellers push back on AI firms buying rare books in bulk
stories.blurb: The suspicion is that the books are bought quietly and destroyed after scanning. A supply chain for training data that runs through physical objects, and the people who sell them are noticing.

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.headline: Booksellers suspect AI firms are buying and then destroying rare books

stories.title: "Everyone can design" comes back, this time from the inside
stories.blurb: The phrase designers have dreaded for years returns, and the argument is that it now cuts the other way: designers no longer have to wait for permission.

sources.name: UX Collective
sources.headline: Design's dreaded phrase is coming back. This time we're in control.

stories.title: Good Screens asks what balanced technology would look like
stories.blurb: It's Nice That Insights reports a growing appetite for devices that do something positive, and looks at how brands can answer that creatively. A brief for anyone designing attention.

sources.name: It's Nice That
sources.headline: How can tech serve us better? Insights explores in new report, Good Screens

stories.title: Borrowed trust is the thing being spent
stories.blurb: The trusted name is the mask, and the machine underneath does not know when it is wrong. The more we trust the name, the less we check, and the more that name stands to lose.

sources.name: UX Collective
sources.headline: We're gorging on borrowed trust and it's going to cost us.

stories.title: A grant program to replace modernism
stories.blurb: Stripe CEO Patrick Collison and economist Tyler Cowen are funding an attempt to define a new look for the 21st century. Taste as a funded project, with the money coming from tech.

sources.name: Fast Company
sources.headline: What should the future look like? Inside the tech-funded program to create a new aesthetic

stories.title: D'Addario admits the promo music came from Suno
stories.blurb: For nearly two weeks the guitar string company denied it, offering explanations from low-quality exports onward, while the evidence piled up. A brand built on instruments got caught generating the sound.

sources.name: The Verge
sources.headline: Guitar company D'Addario admits that AI music was used in a promotional video

stories.title: Jaguar shows the inside of the Type 01
stories.blurb: The Type 00 concept dragged Jaguar into both the car world and the culture war from December 2024 on. The production interior is the first look at what survived the noise.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: Jaguar's new car's interior has been revealed: welcome to the inside of the Type 01

stories.title: Senior creatives are leaving earlier than expected
stories.blurb: Creative Boom picks up a conversation running through the industry about people planning their exit ahead of schedule. Where the experience goes when it goes is the open question.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: Is there a retirement crisis in the creative industry?

stories.title: August hires and launches suggest the floor has been reached
stories.blurb: The monthly roundup of movers, launches and wins reads better than it has in a while, and the editor's takeaway is that things are looking up. One month is not a trend, but it is a data point.

sources.name: Creative Boom
sources.headline: Booms & Shakes: Why August's hires and launches might suggest the worst is behind us
